subject: Data Engineering
title: Duplicate Records
description: A micro-lesson that makes Duplicate Records usable.

hook.text: A customer receives the same marketing email three times. The CRM has three copies of their record.

buildup.text: Duplicates arise from retries, multiple ingestion paths, merging systems, or human data entry.

discovery.text: Exact duplicates are easy to catch. Near-duplicates — 'Jon Smith' vs 'John Smith' — are harder.

twist.text: Dedup after the fact is expensive. Preventing duplicates at ingestion is orders of magnitude cheaper.

climax.text: Natural keys, upsert patterns, and dedup stages at ingestion stop duplicates before they spread.

punchline.text: One record per entity. Simple rule, hard practice.

quiz.question: Why are near-duplicate records harder to fix than exact duplicates?
options: They require fuzzy matching algorithms to detect
